note: Kenya's three largest banks by the Central Bank of Kenya's tier-one ranking are KCB, Equity and Co-op Bank. KCB's card pages and Co-op Bank's tariff guide were read; Equity publishes no card tariff that could be found (only an aggregator's 2021 figures turned up), so Equity isn't written, and Absa Bank Kenya, the next large issuer, was read too: its tariff guide (effective 1 June 2026) gives its cards' annual fees, late, excess, cash advance and 3.00% forex fees but no interest rate, so its cards can't be written. Co-op Bank's tariff guide (charges as of 22 October 2026), read in full: its Classic, Gold and Platinum credit cards cost 3,500, 6,000 and 7,000 shillings a year (the joining fees of 3,000, 3,500 and 4,000 are currently waived, so not written), interest is 3.5% a month on the revolved balance, a late payment costs 1.25% of the minimum payable, a cash advance 6% of the amount, going over the limit 1,000 shillings; the Classic cardholder pays card insurance of 0.39% of the limit a year (the bank pays it for Gold and Platinum). The guide says excise duty applies to all fees without stating its rate, so it isn't written; the 50-day credit cycle isn't written as a grace period; the bonus fee (5% of an amount awarded beyond the limit, only on request) isn't written. The Platinum figures sit in a run the text layer splits, so they were read by eye. KCB Bank Kenya's own product pages for each of its seven personal credit cards (Classic Visa, Gold Mastercard, Gold Visa, Platinum Visa, Visa Signature, Infinite and World Elite; read 30 October 2026, undated): every one charges 3.5% a month and 1,000 shillings over the limit, and its annual fee is written; the joining fees are all waived; the Classic, Gold and Platinum cards' minimum payment is 10% of the billed amount, their late fee 5% of the outstanding balance, their cash advance fee 6%, and they give up to 45 days interest free. The Platinum page calls its 6% cash advance and 5% late charges 'interest'; each is a one-off share of the amount, so they're written as fees. The Infinite card's late fee is 5% of the balance; its cash withdrawal lines (KES 500 at KCB's ATMs, 6% at others, beside a replacement fee of 6%) are garbled, so no cash fee is written for it. The Visa Signature and World Elite pages give a 5% late fee without saying 5% of what, so it isn't written; their cash advance is 6% of the amount. The insurance fee of 0.038% of each amount transacted has no form in the game and isn't written; the pages say charges exclude tax without naming its rate. The KCB Sahl World Elite card's page publishes no rates. Business and corporate cards aren't written. Wave 4 (30 October 2026), for a third bank: Standard Chartered Bank Kenya, a tier-one bank and a long-standing card issuer, was chosen as the next large issuer that publishes its card terms, Equity's being unpublished and Absa Kenya's lacking a rate. Its Service and Price Guide for individual accounts (updated December 2025, the copy its service charges page links), read by eye, as its text is drawn as outlines: its Visa Gold, Platinum and Infinite credit cards (named so on its credit cards page) cost 6,000, 7,000 and 8,000 shillings a year, charge 3.0% a month, 2,000, 3,000 and 3,000 shillings over the limit, 1,500 for a late payment, 5%, 4% and 4% for a cash advance, and 2.5% on spending in another currency, which the guide calls the minimum FX margin (written at 2.5%, the only figure it gives). The guide adds 20% excise duty to its charges under the Finance Act 2023, but not to the credit life insurance, the FX margin or the interest, so it is written as a 20% tax on the fees. The credit life insurance (0.078% a month) is marked optional and isn't written. Stanbic Bank Kenya's credit card page answered a Cloudflare 404 and I&M Bank's a Cloudflare 403; NCBA's cards page wasn't needed.
